selection_reasoning: These four tasks form a coherent multi-hop sequence centered around tree-related materials in a forest scene. The logical flow is: (1) First, the player must find a spruce_sapling, which serves as a landmark/navigation task to locate the spruce area of the scene. (2) Near the spruce area, a spruce_trapdoor is placed that must be mined. (3) The player then navigates to the birch area, where they must mine birch_leaves from a birch tree. (4) Finally, mining birch_wood requires the player to have cleared some leaves first (or approach the trunk), creating a natural dependency on having dealt with the birch_leaves. This creates a branching dependency structure where finding the spruce sapling leads to the trapdoor task, and the birch tasks chain together with leaves before wood.

milestones.description: Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate task. The spruce sapling is placed at spawn-relative (-3, 0, -3). The player must navigate near it and face toward it to demonstrate they have located it. max_distance=16 allows detection from a reasonable distance, and facing_tolerance=60 ensures the player is actually looking at the sapling.

Uses inventory_has because mining a spruce trapdoor always drops itself as an item into the player's inventory. The trapdoor is at (-5, 1, -2) and when broken with the iron axe it will appear in inventory. This is the most direct and reliable check for a mine task where the block drops itself.

Uses count_in_box_at_most (kind='block') because mining birch leaves does NOT reliably drop a leaf block into inventory — leaves typically drop saplings, sticks, or nothing when broken without Silk Touch. Instead, we verify that at least some birch_leaves blocks have been removed from the canopy. The birch leaves span from (3,3,1) to (7,6,5) in spawn-relative coords. The original scene has approximately 48+ birch_leaves blocks; setting max_count=45 ensures at least a few have been mined.

Uses inventory_has because mining birch_wood (the all-bark block variant) always drops itself as an item into the player's inventory. The birch wood trunk spans (5, 0-4, 3) with an additional block at (5, 5, 3). Mining any of these blocks with the iron axe will place birch_wood in inventory. This is the most direct and reliable verification.

scene_description: A flat grass clearing with two distinct tree structures: a spruce area (negative X/Z) with a spruce log trunk, spruce leaves canopy, a spruce sapling on the ground, and a spruce trapdoor attached to the trunk; and a birch area (positive X/Z) with a birch wood trunk, dense birch leaves canopy. Player is given an iron axe to mine all blocks.
task_text: In this forest clearing, find the spruce sapling on the ground near the spruce tree. Then mine the spruce trapdoor attached to the spruce tree trunk. Next, mine some birch leaves from the birch tree canopy. Finally, mine a birch wood block from the birch tree trunk.
design_notes: Spruce area at ~-5,~0,~-3 with spruce log trunk (4 blocks tall), spruce leaves canopy (3x3x3 from y2-y4), spruce sapling at ~-3,~0,~-3, and spruce trapdoor at ~-5,~1,~-2 (facing south, on trunk). Birch area at ~5,~0,~3 with birch wood trunk (5 blocks tall), birch leaves in two layers (3x3x3 from y3-y5 and 5x3x5 from y4-y6), plus a birch wood block at the top (y5). The dependency of leaves-before-wood is supported because the lower birch wood blocks are accessible but the upper ones are surrounded by leaves. Player has iron axe for efficient mining of all materials.
